reason: SBA's 7(a)/504 FOIA release is a direct, no-account, loan-level CSV with a published field dictionary, quarterly vintages, and a 'U.S. Government Works' designation. It yields a genuine forward-looking binary label (charge-off within five years of approval) whose determinants are all recorded at approval, and the FY2010-FY2019 decade file contains fully seasoned cohorts, so chronological train/eval/holdout splits need no imputation of unresolved outcomes. Unlike the already-selected items this is commercial credit risk, a domain not yet represented.
title: Will a newly approved U.S. SBA 7(a) business loan be charged off within five years?

source.publisher: U.S. Small Business Administration (Office of Capital Access)
source.license: U.S. Government Works (SBA metadata 'License' field, linking to the federal public-domain label)
source.attribution: None stated by the publisher; recommended credit: U.S. Small Business Administration, '7(a) & 504 FOIA', data.sba.gov

task.question: At the moment a 7(a) loan is approved, will the loan be charged off within the following 60 months?
task.decision_user: A participating-lender credit officer or SBA Office of Capital Access reviewer deciding whether to extend an SBA-guaranteed 7(a) loan
task.prediction_time: Loan approval date (ApprovalDate). Every input is a field recorded at approval in the same record; no disbursement, status, or servicing field is used.
task.target: Binary: 1 if ChargeOffDate is non-null and ChargeOffDate <= ApprovalDate + 60 months (i.e. LoanStatus CHGOFF observed inside the horizon); 0 otherwise, including PIF, EXEMPT (disbursed and still current), CANCLD, and COMMIT rows whose horizon passed with no charge-off.
task.outcome_horizon: 60 months from ApprovalDate. The latest holdout approval is 2019-09-30, so its window closes 2024-09-30 and every label is resolved in the 2026-09-30 vintage this file carries.

features.name: GrossApproval
features.meaning: Total approved loan amount in dollars
features.availability: Recorded at approval in the same row

features.name: InitialInterestRate
features.meaning: Total initial rate (base plus spread) at approval
features.availability: Dictionary states 'at time loan was approved'

features.name: ProcessingMethod
features.meaning: Program channel used (7AG, PLP, SBX, EXP, CAI, ...)

features.name: BusinessAge
features.meaning: Categorical description of business age (categorical, not a number)

features.name: ProjectState
features.meaning: State where the project is located

features.name: FranchiseCode / FranchiseName
features.meaning: Franchise affiliation, if any (use presence and code, not the name string)

features.name: JobsSupported
features.meaning: Jobs created plus retained as self-reported by the lender on the SBA application

features.name: CollateralInd
features.meaning: Whether the lender reported the loan as collateral-backed

features.name: LocationID
features.meaning: SBA lender identifier; used as a hashed categorical plus a training-window-only lender charge-off rate

features.name: ApprovalMonth
features.meaning: Month-of-year of approval as a seasonality/calendar control

task.population: Every row in the FY2010-FY2019 file with a parseable ApprovalDate inside the split window, GrossApproval > 0, and a parseable 6-digit NaicsCode. No filter uses a post-approval field: CANCLD and COMMIT approvals are retained and receive label 0 because funding status is only knowable after approval. Borrower name/street/city/zip and the current-assignee bank block are dropped, not used as features.
task.split_policy: Fixed boundaries on ApprovalDate, no resampling: train = approvals 2010-10-01 through 2013-09-30 (FY2011-FY2013); embargo = FY2014 (2013-10-01 to 2014-09-30) dropped entirely; eval = 2014-10-01 through 2016-09-30 (FY2015-FY2016); embargo = FY2017 dropped; holdout = 2017-10-01 through 2019-09-30 (FY2018-FY2019), scored once. Thresholds and the feature list are frozen before any holdout scoring. Because the 60-month outcome windows of adjacent cohorts overlap in calendar time, the embargo addresses regime drift rather than label leakage; no row's features are computed from another row's outcome.
task.usefulness: No single field determines the label: charge-off five years later is an administrative event driven jointly by loan structure (size, term, rate type, guaranty share), borrower type and age, industry, geography, franchise status, and the approval channel the lender used. The label is only observable years after the features, so the task exercises real temporal generalization, and the ProcessingMethod and lender contrasts are a live policy question about which guaranty channels carry risk.
task.simple_references: Majority class (overall, and per split); NAICS 2-digit sector crossed with GrossApproval decile, with base rates estimated on the training window only; lender-level historical charge-off rate by LocationID estimated on the training window only; fixed approval-year dummies as a drift control. Persistence does not apply: each row is a distinct loan with no repeated-unit history.

evidence.claim: The publisher exposes loan-level 7(a) CSVs segmented by decade plus a data dictionary, refreshed quarterly, with the license recorded as U.S. Government Works.
evidence.quote: There are four files for the 7(a) loan program that segment the data by decade.

evidence.claim: The release is maintained quarterly rather than being a one-off extract.
evidence.quote: The FOIA data for the 7(a) and 504 programs are updated quarterly.

evidence.claim: Charge-off timing is a documented field separate from approval, which makes a forward-looking label possible.
evidence.quote: ChargeOffDate,Date SBA charged off loan (if applicable)

evidence.claim: LoanStatus enumerates the codes used to build and audit the label.
The interest rate feature is explicitly an approval-time quantity, not a current one.
evidence.quote: Initial interest rate - total interest rate (base rate plus spread) at time loan was approved

evidence.claim: BankName describes the current assignee, so the bank block is post-approval and must be excluded as input.
evidence.quote: Name of the bank that the loan is currently assigned to

evidence.claim: The FOIA extract is loan-level and covers the full approval history, so decade cohorts can be built without a join.
evidence.quote: These reports provide loan-level data on all 7(a) & 504 loans approved since FY1991.

evidence.claim: The license target page is the federal guidance on works of U.S. government employees, supporting redistribution as a government work.
evidence.quote: Government work is something created by a U.S. government officer or employee as part of their official duties.

construction.format: CSV, one row per approved 7(a) loan, header row, about 42 columns mixing dollars, integers, short code strings and dates. Dates are ISO-style in at least the AsOfDate field; parse ApprovalDate and ChargeOffDate with a tolerant parser and coerce amounts and term to numeric with errors='coerce'.
construction.access_recipe: curl -L -o sba_7a_2010_2019.csv https://data.sba.gov/sites/default/files/uploaded_resources/FOIA_7a_FY2010_FY2019_asof_260930.csv ; then pandas.read_csv(path, dtype=str, low_memory=False) and drop BorrName, BorrStreet, BorrCity, BorrState, BorrZip, BankName, BankFDICNumber, BankNCUANumber, BankStreet, BankCity, BankState, BankZip, plus the outcome columns LoanStatus, PaidInFullDate, ChargeOffDate, GrossChargeOffAmount, and the post-approval columns FirstDisbursementDate and SoldSecMrktInd. Build the label from ChargeOffDate and ApprovalDate, then write train/eval/holdout CSVs on the fixed date boundaries. The separate FY2020-present file is not needed and should not be concatenated.
construction.expected_size: Explicitly estimated, not downloaded in this session: roughly 5 to 6 hundred thousand rows and 250-400 MB for the FY2010-FY2019 decade file. A third-party methodology note reports the sibling FY2020-present file at 388,338 rows and 42 columns, which bounds the per-row width; the older decade is expected to be the larger of the two. Restricting to the three split windows leaves roughly 400,000 rows.
construction.source_examples: Dictionary-documented value sets to assert on ingest: ProcessingMethod codes 7AG, 7EW, WCP, SGC, CAI, CAT, CAR, CRL, CTR, EXP, ITR, MAC, PLP, PLW, PWC, SBX, SLC, STC; LoanStatus codes CANCLD, CHGOFF, COMMIT, EXEMPT, PIF; RevolverStatus 0=Term and 1=Revolver; BusinessType Individual, Partnership, or Corporation. Sanity checks: LoanStatus values are a subset of the five codes; ChargeOffDate is populated only where LoanStatus is CHGOFF; SBAGuaranteedApproval never exceeds GrossApproval; ApprovalFY agrees with the year of ApprovalDate. A third-party research note (dunelandfinancial.com, not the publisher) additionally reports 42 columns, AsOfDate 2026-06-30 on an earlier vintage, and a non-numeric BusinessAge value 'Change of Ownership'; treat that as a lead to verify, not as documentation.

limitations: Current-vintage reconstruction: the file is a 2026-09-30 snapshot, so approval-time features are recovered from a later extract. This does not prove the fields looked identical operationally at each approval, and later corrections to early rows are invisible to us.
Approved-only selection: no denied applications are in the file, so the model estimates charge-off risk conditional on approval and cannot be used as an underwriting model on raw applicants.

No unique loan identifier exists in the extract (the dictionary lists no loan ID), so duplicates cannot be deduplicated and the same borrower may recur; because borrower name and address are dropped for privacy, repeated-borrower grouping is not possible and a small amount of cross-split borrower overlap is unavoidable.

Lender clustering is strong: many loans share a LocationID, and lender behavior partly determines both approval mix and loss outcomes, so rows are not fully independent and holdout lenders may be unseen in training.

Charge-off is an administrative loss-recognition event that lags delinquency and depends on SBA and lender practice, so it is a noisy proxy for economic default and its timing conventions may shift across the decade.

Cancelled and undisbursed approvals are scored as label 0 by construction to avoid using a post-decision funding field for eligibility; this makes the label mean 'approved loan that ends in charge-off', not 'funded loan that defaults'.
JobsSupported and BusinessAge are self-reported and explicitly unvalidated by SBA, and BusinessAge is categorical with at least one non-numeric category, so it cannot be treated as years in business.

The source carries business names and street addresses (sole proprietors can be individuals). Our contribution must drop those columns and release only derived features plus an opaque row key; upstream rights and the FOIA basis are unchanged by that de-identification.
The 60-month outcome windows of adjacent cohorts overlap in calendar time, so a macro shock can affect two splits at once; the embargo reduces but does not remove this dependence.
Redistribution applies to the U.S. Government Works source; any CC0 designation covers only our derived contribution and does not relicense upstream material.
